summary: Masatoshi Nagatomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard University (Ph.D. ~1951-1957), where he was Instructor of Sanskrit (1958) and Professor (1969).

Masayuki Taira works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970-1978) and held posts at Kansai University (~1982-1989), Osaka University (~1989-2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2017).

Massimo Pallottino was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927-1931), later holding posts at the University of Cagliari (~1945-1947) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1947-1980).
Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Mochizuki held posts at Minobusan University as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as a professor (attested 2015).

Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He became a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992.
Matteo Bartoli was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1894-1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1899-1900). He held a post at the University of Turin from ~1908 to 1946.

Matthew B. Orsborn is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisors Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, and studied under traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang (all attested 2012).

Matthew Immergut is a scholar in religious studies and sociology who studied under Culadasa. He held a post as Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York (attested 2011).

Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Toronto (-2014) supervised by Frances Garrett, and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thupten Champa.

Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008) and held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Helen Baroni and Michel Mohr, and a PhD at Duke University under Richard M. Jaffe (attested 2015).

Matthew T. Kapstein is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. at Brown University (1980-1987) and held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University (~1989-1996), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (2002).
Matthias de Vries was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1838-1843). He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849-1853) and Leiden University (1853-1891).

Matthias von Lexer was a linguist who earned a PhD at Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1858-1860). He held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1868-1870), the University of Würzburg (1868), and the University of Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a doctorate in molecular biology at the Pasteur Institute (~1967-1972) under François Jacob, and studied under traditional teachers Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse.

Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski (~2004-2009). He held posts at International Buddhist College (~2009-2013) and Mahidol University (~2013).

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and was a Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).

Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman, earning a PhD from Johns Hopkins University (~1878-1879). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.
Maurice Grammont was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1888-1892). He held a post at the University of Montpellier from ~1895 to 1939.
Maurice Jametel was a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École des langues orientales and later held a post there from ~1886 to 1889.
